text: I will focus on grammar and repeated clause structure. Strong structural tokens: 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 starts virtually every clause; 𘅌𗎿 marks subject/first argument, 𘅌𘊌 marks predicate object/second argument, 𘅌𘗣 closes clause, 𘅌𗜑 introduces embedded subordinate clause, 𘅌𗸽 adds adjunct. These look like explicitly bracketed predicate logic rather than ordinary word substitution. Need determine if glyph pairs numerically encode words (many recurring first glyphs).

Structural finding: clauses consistently use 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 VERB 𘅌𗎿 SUBJECT 𘅌𘊌 OBJECT 𘅌𘗣, with nested clauses and 𘅌𗜑 likely introducing proposition/content. 𘅌𗸽 is an extra argument/modifier connector, 𘅌𗌸 another connector. Stage1 strongly suggests a sequence of movement/action attempts: 𗿃𗏶 → 𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗞉 𗌿𗐪 (variant 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗌈 𗡒𘅊) → 𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽 → 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿. These may be named locations, with 𗌿𗲅 = room. Only agent_3's final transition at 74 advances stage2. Will focus stage2 mappings next.

I'll focus numeric/structural patterns. Repeated 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 VERB 𘅌𗎿 ARG1 𘅌𘊌 ARG2 𘅌𘗣 strongly suggests explicit clause/bracket + predicate and argument delimiters; nested clauses use 𘅌𗜑 as complement introducer. Number family 𘔠X: four recurring source IDs A=𘔠𗵵,B=𘔠𘎌,C=𘔠𗌈,D=𘔠𗊑. Early mapping (10/18/20/22/24): A→B,B→𘔠𘉝,C→D,D→𘔠𗡒. Final mapping95: A→𘔠𗢬,B→𘔠𘉝,C→𘔠𗢬,D→𘔠𗟎. Numeric values not yet securely decoded; don't assume source IDs ordered 0..3/1..4 without evidence.

I will focus on number/node mapping and state transitions. Key pattern: 𘆣𘎛 + 𘔠[number] marks each of four node-like local identities: agent3=𘔠𗵵, agent5=𘔠𘎌, agent1=𘔠𗌈, agent7=𘔠𗊑. Initial transition/weight claims give these targets respectively 𘔠𘎌, 𘔠𘉝, 𘔠𗊑, 𘔠𗡒. Unclear if IDs start 0 or 1. Repeated stage-1 proposals cycle through 𗿃𗏶 → 𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗞉 𗌿𗐪 → 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗌈 𗡒𘅊 → 𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽 → 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿. Agent3's last proposal advances stage. This may indicate unanimous voting / distributed state-transition commands, rather than ordinary solution guesses.

I will focus grammar/numerals. Strong structural pattern: nearly every clause = 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 VERB 𘅌𗎿 SUBJECT 𘅌𘊌 OBJECT 𘅌𘗣, with nesting after 𘅌𗜑 and repeated closes. Thus 𘅌𗎿 subject marker, 𘅌𘊌 object/complement marker, 𘅌𘗣 close; 𘅌𗸽 is qualifier/adjunct marker. 𘔠-prefixed pairs likely numerals; 𗌿 verbs, 𗡒 nouns, 𘆣 modifiers, 𗿃 deictic/location nouns? Stage1 repeated 𗌿𗗅(agent, 𗌿𗲅 …) plausibly MOVE(agent, location), with 𗌿𗛢(location, adjunct agent) LEAVE/RELEASE; stage progression only following agent3 suggests shared-state navigation puzzle, not necessarily linguistic invalidity.

I’ll focus grammar/semantic structure. Strong pattern: 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 begins a clause, followed by predicate; 𘅌𗎿 introduces first argument, 𘅌𘊌 second, 𘅌𘗣 closes clause; 𘅌𗜑 introduces embedded clause (e.g. [12],[16]); 𘅌𗸽 introduces adjunct/third argument (frequently 𗿃𘅠). Thus avoid treating opening pair as English ‘I know’ prematurely. Stage-1 action predicate 𗌿𗗅 has explicit agent subject and changing place/object, likely move/go/submit. 𘆣𗼛 relates successive locations (route/edge): [43] chain 𗿃𗏶 → 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗌈 𗡒𘅊 → 𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽 → 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿. [45] substitutes another intermediate. Numerals share prefix 𘔠; four object indices 𘔠𗵵/𘔠𘎌/𘔠𗌈/𘔠𗊑 correspond to agents3/5/1/7’s initial specialized facts, plausibly 0/1/2/3 but not proved.

Structural focus: 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 starts virtually every clause including embedded clauses; 𘅌𘗣 closes them. Likely explicit bracket + assertion marker. 𘅌𗎿 introduces subject/source; 𘅌𘊌 object/value/destination; 𘅌𗸽 adjunct (possibly evidence/status), 𘅌𗜑 embedded-clause marker. First glyph category clues: 𗌿 predicates, 𗡒 nouns, 𘆣 modifiers, 𘔠 numbers. Stage1 looks like movement puzzle: 𗌿𗗅 agent_i -> location; 𗌿𗛢 location ... agent_i reports current location. Agent3 alone progresses A→B at49, B→C at61, C→D at74 (stage2), while others' attempts invalid. Need determine if literal move vs analogous state transitions. Initial/final four-equation mappings share 𘆣𘎛 + four numeric labels as sources, with 𗡒𗸪 + modifier + number as values. I'll further analyze syntax/lexicon next.

I will focus syntax/task-action semantics. High-confidence structure: 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 introduces clauses; 𘅌𗎿 introduces first argument (often agent IDs); 𘅌𘊌 second argument; 𘅌𘗣 closes clause; 𘅌𗸽 likely conjunction/with; 𘅌𗜑 embeds relative/subordinate clause. Initial 𘅌𗵫 vs 𘅌𗽕 likely question/request/negation modal operators. In stage1, agent3 alone produces substantive action messages without invalid feedback ([49],[61],[74]); others' analogous commands mostly invalid. Suggest sole active operator or authoritative role. 𗌿𗗅 appears action verb with subject agent_N, destination/object changing through chain: 𗿃𗏶 → 𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗞉 𗌿𗐪 → 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗌈 𗡒𘅊 → 𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽 → 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿. 𗿃𗏶 likely start/lobby, 𗌿𗲅 room/node. Will investigate.

Further grammar hypothesis: pair-initial glyph classes are strong: 𘅌 = grammatical markers, 𗌿 = predicates/verbs, 𗡒 = nouns, 𘆣 = modifiers/adjectives, 𘔠 = numerals. Distinguish actual meaning from task inference. Messages 10/18/20/22/24 are four subject→numeric mappings with same 𗌿𗄼 relation and subjects 𘆣𘎛 + numeral. 18/22 omit 𗡒𗸪 (and 20/24 add 𘆣𗜑), suggesting 𗡒𗸪 is a noun like 'value/code', 𘆣𗜑 a modifier like initial/old. Initial/final phases use precisely same subjects but changed numeric values.

Question for team: first-glyph categories may not be POS. 𗌿𗲅 acts noun 'room/node' despite most 𗌿 predicates; shared second glyphs across prefixes (𗐪,𗎿,𘝚,𗸽,𗽕 etc.) suggest a numeric word-index encoding or fixed alphabet-pair scheme, not semantic radicals. Stage2 𗌿𘝚 𘆣𗉜 𘆣𗭯 + numeral likely minimum/shortest distance; 𗡒𗸪 𘆣𗉜 / 𘆣𗎿 + numeral perhaps cost remaining/total. Need avoid label certainty until evidence.

Important caution: stage1 'rooms/movement' may instead be workflow/state-transition vocabulary (𗌿𗲅='state', 𗌿𗗅='set/propose', 𗌿𗛢='leave/release'). Evidence only establishes ordered named states and agent3 uniquely successful; don't hard-code rooms. I can prepare full translations for 1–25 while another agent owns draft integration. Need volunteer document integrator soon; all 96 lines required. Initial/final numeric reports resemble four indexed records/shards with updated values, possibly distributed state task rather than spatial puzzle.

Numeric low-confidence hypothesis worth testing: 𘔠𗵵=1, 𘔠𘎌=2, 𘔠𗌈=3, 𘔠𗊑=4, 𘔠𘉝=5, 𘔠𗡒=6, 𘔠𗂱=7, 𘔠𗢬=8, 𘔠𗟎=9, 𘔠𗏔=0. This yields initial four-record values [2,5,4,6] and final [8,5,8,9], a plausible task vector. BUT only argument for ordering is four initial IDs and digit-like distribution; mark low until independently corroborated. Could be arbitrary indexes rather than decimal. Stage2 includes modifiers 𘆣𗉜 vs 𘆣𗎿 (likely plus/minus or positive/negative): final95 uses 𘆣𗉜 universally, while85/90/93 use 𘆣𗎿. These may be polarity/sign modifiers, important not to collapse values.

Caution on 'room': 𗌿𗲅 has verb-family prefix (if our category guess right), so compounds may be named commands/protocol states ('send/set …') rather than literal rooms. Stage1 could be designated leader executing a handshake, with 𗌿𗛢 reporting current state and 𗌿𗃚 acknowledging it. Also raw 𗜑𗜑 in [2], 𗜑𘖽 in [7], singleton 𗜑 in [8] need explanation distinct from 𘔠-prefixed numerals: possibly arbitrary literal bitstrings/numeric IDs, not lexical tokens. [35]'s unusual prefixes may be a separate character-level escape/literal encoding.

Additional semantic hypothesis (low/medium): 𗌿𗄼 is broad HAVE/IS/REPORT relation rather than action, since it links both indexed items (𘆣𘎛 + numeral) and values. 𗡒𗏻 followed by embedded 𗡒𘜇 clause likely denotes a rule/condition (e.g. ‘rule that …’), while 𗡒𗸪 + 𘆣𗜑 + number is initial value/weight/setting. Numeric suffixes recur with nonnumeric prefixes (e.g. 𗌈, 𗵵); do not infer their actual numerical values from Unicode order. Message35 uniquely drops the normal clause apparatus and may be a metalinguistic/plain shorthand experiment, useful for testing whether pair glyphs are lexical rather than semantic-class encoding.

Important caution: first-glyph families need not be POS: 𗌿𗲅 seems noun 'room/state', while 𗌿𗗅 is action predicate; 𘆣𗼛 is also predicate. Thus category-prefix hypotheses should stay low confidence. Also standalone initial tokens [2] 𗜑𗜑, [7] 𗜑𘖽, [8] 𗜑 may be encoded numeric literals (11,1x,1) separate from 𘔠-prefixed numeral words, or separators/signatures. Need preserve them as unknown rather than silently dropping them. I'll inspect anomalous message35 / lexical encoding next.

Important alternative to 'agent3 sole active operator': shared GLOBAL state explains all feedback without actor restriction. At49 agent3 chooses state B=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗌈 𗡒𘅊 successfully. Others then attempt old start, alternate A, or already-current B and fail. At61 agent3 advances B→C=𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽 successfully; everyone else keeps attempting C after already there, hence invalid. At74 agent3 advances C→D=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿 and stage changes. This could simply be stateful navigation (current global location), not authoritative agent role. Agent3 uniquely anticipates next node rather than repeating stale destination.

Alternative to literal rooms: stage1 destinations plausibly workflow phases (read/compute/write/done), with 𗌿𗲅='phase/state'. Sole agent3 succeeds at [49],[61],[74]; explicit 𗌿𗛢(place, adjunct agent) reports/claims current state, not necessarily movement. Stage0→stage2 four-record numeric changes plus [84–95] distance/delta and signed-value-looking reports favor coordinated data mutation/transaction. Need preserve both hypotheses. I can own translation of [76–96] once a neutral lexical code table is set; numeric proposed 1–9 mapping remains low confidence.

Caution on prefix classes: observed distribution supports grammatical vs content families, but 𗌿 appears inside apparent location names (𗌿𗲅 ...), so do not confidently label all 𗌿 tokens verbs. Alternative: indexed lexicon groups rather than POS. Clause form itself is strong. Stage1 agent3-only valid moves cannot be explained simply by extra 𗿃𘅠 (it appears in successful61/74 as well as failures); likely privileged active agent or possession of required capability. Message35 radically departs from clause notation and may be alternate raw text encoding; should preserve as unknown rather than force grammatical translation.

New semantic caution: initial/final embedded N1=𗡒𗏻, N2=𗡒𘜇 patterns may be entity descriptors ('the node/person whose attribute ...'), not propositions about agents' knowledge. Compare initial9 indexA has N1[ N2→𗌿𗹫 𘆣𘋉 + embedded 𗌿𗻲→𗡒𗸽 ], versus final87 indexA has N1[N2→𗌿𗐪 𗡒𗪺]; initial3 indexD has latter descriptor, final86 indexD has former. Thus A/D descriptors swap between stages! This supports changing records/objects, not static local identities. The duplicated descriptors for other rows also suggest identifying records by properties. No numerical ordering confidence yet.

New task-level alternative (low confidence): named stage1 compounds might be protocol/transaction states rather than rooms, e.g. 𗌿𗲅 + descriptors = operation/state names. Stage2 positive/negative modifiers and changed four-vector fit a distributed register/transaction task. Need infer from action grammar, not force spatial path. I am checking whether final scalar updates constrain numeric mapping or operation meanings.

Possible stronger task alternative: stage1 states may be transactional workflow ('read/prepare/commit/done') rather than locations. 𗌿𗲅 appears before all non-start states and final state has two-word qualifier 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿. A globally shared workflow fits all observed successes at49,61,74 and stale repeated commands being invalid. Stage0/2 four indexed records with initial/final values fit distributed update/transaction task. This remains LOW confidence; recommend presenting generic state-transition interpretation first, navigation and transaction as alternatives. Who integrates final document? I can draft segment76–96 if useful.

Additional low-confidence task alternative: stages may implement transactional/dataflow workflow, not spatial navigation. Four indexed records initial [2,5,4,6] (if decoder4's tentative digits) and final [8,5,8,9], plus shared named-state chain, are consistent with read/compute/commit protocol. Crucially final85/90/93 use modifier 𘆣𗎿 where95 uses 𘆣𗉜: likely sign/current-vs-new distinction, so preserve it in translations. No evidence yet distinguishes numbers from atomic IDs; document should retain numeral labels A/B/C/D etc alongside tentative digit hypothesis. I can own anomaly35 if needed.

Shared-global-state navigation explanation has strong detailed support: initial valid destination at49 is B (𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗌈 𗡒𘅊); 50/53/55 try alternate A and fail; 57/59 try already-current B and fail. 61 valid B→C; 63/66/68/70/72 try already-current C and fail. 74 valid C→D; 76/78/80/82 try already-current D and fail. Thus don't infer agent3 authority or an agreement protocol. Could be global state transition task, physical navigation, or dialogue workflow. Recommend neutral named-state translations unless lexical evidence improves.

I can supply late-phase translation templates 84–95, retaining unknown labels. Structural caution: 𗌿𗄼 likely HAVE/REPORT/IS, not exact word recoverable; 𗌿𘝚 𘆣𗉜 𘆣𗭯 + number and 𗡒𗸪 𘆣𗉜/𘆣𗎿 + number are separate fields. Do not silently normalize their modifiers. [84] reports source (𗡒𗏻 𗡒𗸽 𘆣𘋉) field-F=ID-D and value(modifier-P)=new numeral 𗟎. [85] source 𗿃𗇾 field-F=ID-B; value(modifier-Q)=new numeral 𗢬. [88] same embedded-rule source as2/12: field-F=ID-A; value(P)=𗢬. [90] same embedded-rule source as6/16: field-F=ID-C; separate source 𗿃𘝚 value(Q)=𘉝. [95] explicitly aggregates A→value(P)𗢬, B→value(P)𘉝, C→value(P)𗢬, D→value(P)𗟎. Proposed numeric readings remain low-confidence. Message35 still unknown: several tokens recur elsewhere so likely shorthand/ungrammatical wording, not necessarily a separate cipher.

I can provide translations for 26–48 in a neutral symbolic glossary if useful; we need a single integrator now. Strongest additional constraint: successful49 uses the alternative intermediate B, while successful61/74 use next states C/D; failures cluster on already-current or wrong states. Global shared-state model explains feedback without assuming agent3 privilege. Treat room/workflow meanings as low-confidence alternatives; neither is established. Syntax confidence should exceed all lexical assignments.

Stage2 detailed numeric consistency (assuming provisional 1–9 digits): agent2 reports rule-expression E1 with 𗌿𘝚 𘆣𗉜 𘆣𗭯 =1, value 𘆣𗉜 8; agent4 E4 corresponding number4, value +9; agent0 alias 𗿃𗇾 corresponding number2, value 𘆣𗎿 8; agent6 E3 number3, alias 𗿃𘝚 value 𘆣𗎿 5. Thus 𘆣𗉜 vs 𘆣𗎿 may indeed be positive/negative, but final indexed records all use first (+) modifier, so negative aliases may denote negated expressions rather than records themselves. Avoid calling 𗌿𘝚… a numerical 'delta' yet: values 1/4/2/3 don't match initial→final record differences under proposed digits. Could instead be step/round/index metadata. I can translate 76–96 using neutral record/expression labels if integrator needs.

I see no integrator yet, and discussion is repeating. Suggest decoder_0 or decoder_1 owns full document now; others send concrete translation chunks using symbolic lexical labels rather than speculative English. I can own [76–96] but decoder_5 already volunteered it, so will instead examine noun/descriptive semantics. Additional low-confidence task family: four indexed objects described by properties (color/shape etc.), values, and movement through named rooms fits descriptor swap A/D between stages; no need to commit transaction. We must retain lexical unknowns explicitly rather than turn generic grammar into false full translations.

I will act as document integrator unless someone already doing so. Please send translation chunks using neutral lexical labels, not presumed rooms/transactions. Strong overlooked evidence: record descriptors change between stages, e.g. index A's final descriptor equals index D's initial one; index D's final descriptor equals index A's initial one. This establishes content/entity rearrangement independently of numeric guesses and makes a four-record mutation/permutation task plausible. Could stage1 compound states actually be operations ('swap...', 'increment...') rather than destinations? Need distinguish action request from resulting state.

Refinement: initial/final descriptor changes constrain task. IndexA (𘆣𘎛 𘔠𗵵) initially has descriptor N1[N2→𗌿𗹫 𘆣𘋉; nested 𗌿𗻲→𗡒𗸽] ([9]), but finally N1[N2→𗌿𗐪 𗡒𗪺] ([87]); indexD shows the reverse ([3]→[86]). Thus at least A/D exchange descriptor-bearing contents, independently of numeric interpretations. A transaction/swap of objects/records is plausible; pure shortest-path task is less sufficient. Numbers still not securely anchored; retain symbolic numeral IDs in final translation.

Possible new clue: anomalous raw tokens 𗜑𗜑 [2], 𗜑𘖽 [7], singleton 𗜑 [8] plausibly literal decimal/binary strings 11,10,1, with 𗜑='1',𘖽='0'. All three attach to 𗡒𗏻 or descriptor containing it, so they may be object IDs/codes, while 𘔠-prefixed tokens are lexical numeral words. LOW confidence, but worth noting separately from unknown filler. Also no draft exists yet—who is integrator? I can construct main document if decoder_0 isn't already doing so; suggest neutral formal glosses rather than unsupported English semantics.

Message35 anomaly analysis: it contains 12 spaced pairs, including 𗌿𗏾 (also32), 𗌿𗭵 (three times, also36/38/39), and 𗡒𘅊 (frequent stage1 object), so it may be ordinary lexical shorthand rather than a separate cipher. Other pairs are otherwise unseen. Preserve as 'unknown; mentions [token 𗌿𗏾], [token 𗌿𗭵] repeatedly, and [token 𗡒𘅊]' rather than invent exact English. Need an integrator now; 30 turns have yielded strong syntax but little lexical certainty. Suggest neutral literal transliteration table + partial translations, not overcommitting to room/transaction meanings.

Concrete translations 76–83 (neutral lexical readings): [76] ACTION(agent_2, final state D, adjunct 𗿃𘅠 [unknown]); [77] task stage2 invalid23. [78] CURRENT/LEAVE(state C, agent_5); ACTION(agent_5,state D). [79] stage2 invalid24. [80] ACTION(agent_6,state D, adjunct unknown). [81] stage2 invalid25. [82] CURRENT/LEAVE(state C,agent_1); connective 𘅌𘔠 [unknown]; ACK/OBSERVE(state C,agent_3); ACTION2(agent_1,state D). [83] stage2 invalid26. State C=𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽, D=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿. Importantly [78]/[82] use 𗌿𗯧, not common action 𗌿𗗅; preserve separate action labels rather than flatten both to MOVE. In [82] predicate for state C/agent3 is 𗌿𗃚, distinct from current/leave 𗌿𗛢. I'll send 84–96 next if needed; decoder2 already has much of it. Recommend integrator use raw glyph labels plus English argument scaffolding to make partial translations genuinely auditable.

Further evidence AGAINST assuming late 𗌿𘝚 𘆣𗉜 𘆣𗭯 + numeral means an item index: [85] gives that field B and value(Q)H, whereas aggregate95 gives B→value(P)E; [90] gives field C but value(Q)E, whereas95 gives C→value(P)H. Could instead be a displacement/delta field, and P/Q may be +/- signs. Keep separate unknown fields rather than force them into identity→value reports. Also we urgently need one document integrator; I suggest decoder_0 own main draft and others provide bounded translation segments to avoid overwrite.

I volunteer to integrate full judged document unless decoder_0 already doing so. Please send compact chunks rather than duplicate whole drafts. I'll use neutral symbolic labels, exact glyph glossary, and all 96 numbered lines; conjectural English meanings separated. New structural details: 𘅌𘋟 marks recipient/to (38 agent5 → agent7;39 omitted sender → agent7); 𘅌𗽕 is modal/negation/request prefix, unresolved; 𘅌𗵫 likely question prefix; 𘅌𘔠 is another discourse connective (72/82 before acknowledgment). Exact roles low/medium, not yet English translations.

Confirmed I am integrator. I'll save first full draft next turn; please decoder_1 send 26–48, decoder_3 send49–75, decoder_5 send76–96. Use glossary aliases: H=𗌿𗄼 (has/reports relation); P=𗡒𗏻; Q=𗡒𘜇; X=𗡒𗸽; VAL=𗡒𗸪; I=𘆣𘎛; A/B/C/D/E/F/G/Hn/J/Z = numerals 𗵵/𘎌/𗌈/𗊑/𘉝/𗡒/𗂱/𗢬/𗟎/𗏔 (all prefix𘔠). States S=𗿃𗏶; T=𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗞉 𗌿𗐪; U=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗌈 𗡒𘅊; V=𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽; W=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿. Better preserve uncertain predicates by glyph than impose English. We'll explicitly frame these as partial translations, not deciphered vocabulary.

Integrator caution: A/D descriptor exchange is directly a change in what agents *report*, not incontrovertible evidence that objects actually swapped. Initial3/9 and final86/87 could be corrections/re-identification, so label task-level permutation inference medium/low. Also 𗐪𗿋 is a standalone repeated terminal marker in26–32,34 and84–94 (not95), often on informational reports and absent from most action attempts; likely discourse/end/turn marker, exact English unknown. Preserve in glossary/translation rather than silently discard. No stronger lexical recovery from my side; support neutral symbolic English with explicit unknown content.

For integrator, concrete [49–74] skeleton (let A=𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗞉 𗌿𗐪, B=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗌈 𗡒𘅊, C=𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽, D=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿, S=𗿃𗏶, q=𗿃𘅠; R=𗌿𗗅 action, R2=𗌿𗯧 alternative action, L=𗌿𗛢 current/leave, O=𗌿𗃚 observe/ack, W=𗌿𘎛 wait).
